_comment: Known wire differences between this port and upstream abap2UI5 running on
open-abap (scripts/conformance.js). A NEW key is a regression; a key that no
longer reproduces must be delisted. Regenerate the KEY SET with --update, then
write the reasons by hand — an unexplained entry is a bug with a green build in
break    — the port is WRONG and the shipped package is affected. Requires
`tracked`, naming where the fix is planned. These are not accepted;
they are enumerated so the gate can stay green while they are
worked off, exactly as the units ratchet does.
accepted — a difference somebody chose, with the reason why.
THE FIRST RUN OF THIS GATE (2026-09-18) FOUND A SHIPPED PROTOCOL BREAK.
All 21 entries below reduce to FOUR causes, and two of them mean the
published cap2UI5 app cannot render at all: the mirrored webapp reads
S_FRONT.S_ACTION and the engine writes S_FRONT.PARAMS. See

hi_world::init::.MODEL.NAME.why: The upstream side of the same flattening — MODEL.NAME exists there and is absent here. Listed separately from MODEL.XX so that a fix which flattens the model but forgets to drop the XX wrapper (or vice versa) still shows one open entry.

hi_world::init::.MODEL.XX.why: The port nests two-way bindings under MODEL.XX and binds them as {/XX/NAME}. Upstream flattened this: the binding is {/NAME} and the value sits at MODEL.NAME. Because the view XML carries the binding path, a frontend built for flat paths cannot resolve a model the backend nested — the field silently stays empty rather than erroring.

hi_world::init::.S_FRONT.APP.why: Upstream echoes the app class name upper-cased (Z2UI5_CL_UI5_APP_HI_WORLD) because ABAP class names are upper case; the port echoes the lower-case JS module name. The webapp's hash router writes this value into the URL route '#/app/<CLASS>' and compares it on the way back, so a case difference is a route that never matches — not a display nicety. Cheapest of the three causes to fix and the one with no design question attached.

hi_world::init::.S_FRONT.PARAMS.why: The other half of the S_ACTION migration: the port emits PARAMS.S_VIEW.XML where upstream emits an action row ['VIEW_SLOTS','display','MAIN', xml]. Same single root cause as the S_ACTION entry; listed separately because the diff is per field and delisting must be per field.

hi_world::init::.S_FRONT.S_ACTION.why: Upstream delivers every frontend instruction through S_FRONT.S_ACTION as an ordered action table (T_SYSTEM for framework actions, T_CUSTOM for app-issued ones). The port still emits the superseded S_FRONT.PARAMS record. The shipped webapp is mirrored 1:1 from upstream and reads S_ACTION — `grep -c PARAMS core/app/z2ui5/webapp/core/Server.js` is 0 — so this is not a cosmetic envelope difference, it is the frontend and the backend of the SAME published package speaking different protocols.

hi_world::init::view:MAIN.why: The rendered view differs from upstream's at character 108: upstream's <mvc:View> carries displayBlock="true" height="100%" and this port's did not, so the Shell renders in a collapsed box instead of filling the window. FIXED in src/ (2026-09-18) but still listed, because core/ is frozen at the last green build and cannot be rebuilt until ADR-006 worklist item 4 is closed — delist it once a rebuilt core ships the fix. The port also differs on _bind_edit vs upstream's _bind, which is deliberately NOT fixed here: it is coupled to the model-shape migration (worklist item 2).
hi_world::init::view:MAIN.tracked: docs/adr-006-conformance.md — worklist item 4 (rebuild), fix already in src/

hi_world::post-event::.MODEL.why: Upstream sends NO MODEL key at all when the model did not change on this roundtrip — Server.js reads that absence as MODELPRESENT=false and skips the model push. The port sends the full model every time. Beyond the shape mismatch this is a wire-size and a correctness difference: an unconditional push overwrites frontend-side edits the user made after the request left.

hi_world::post-event::.S_FRONT.APP.why: Same casing difference on the event path. Separate entry because the value is composed in a different branch; a fix applied only to the init path would leave this one open, which is the point of listing per field.

hi_world::post-event::.S_FRONT.PARAMS.why: The port's PARAMS.S_MSG_BOX record for the same message box. Note the payload differs beyond the envelope: the port carries CLOSEONNAVIGATION and TYPE='information', upstream carries a {title:'Information'} options object — so the migration is a re-shaping of each action's arguments, not a rename of the wrapper.

hi_world::post-event::.S_FRONT.S_ACTION.why: Same migration on the event path: upstream answers a message box as T_CUSTOM [['MESSAGE_BOX','show', text, {title}]]. Kept as its own entry because the event path builds its actions in a different branch of the handler than the init path, so it can be fixed — or broken — independently.

start_page::init::.MODEL.MS_HOME.BTN_EVE.why: The port publishes an attribute it never bound. Upstream's MS_HOME carries exactly the eight fields the app binds (btn_icon, btn_text, class_editable, class_value_state, class_value_state_text, classname, link_enabled, url); btn_event_id is passed to _event( ) and to nothing else, so it is not in upstream's model. The port's model carries it anyway, which says the port publishes the whole structure rather than what was bound - the same mechanism, unproven but strongly suggested, behind the rest of the model-shape differences. It also binds two fields fewer than upstream (classname, link_enabled), so the two sides disagree in both directions. Fix the publishing rule, not this field.

start_page::init::.MODEL.MS_HOME.CLASSNA.why: Upstream answers Z2UI5_CL_UI5_APP_HI_WORLD, the port z2ui5_cl_ui5_app_hi_world - the same casing difference as S_FRONT.APP, one level down, and it is user-visible: the start page shows this string in its input field. Upstream normalises with c_trim_upper( ) where it accepts a class name and rtti_get_classname_by_ref( ) answers upper case; the port carries whatever spelling it was handed. Fixing S_FRONT.APP without fixing this would leave the page showing one spelling and the wire carrying another.

start_page::init::.MODEL.XX.why: The start page's two-way bindings under the XX wrapper, same root cause as hi_world::init::.MODEL.XX. Kept separate because the start page is a framework-owned app whose hand-port may be fixed independently of the engine's generic model builder.

start_page::init::.S_FRONT.APP.why: Same casing difference for the start page. Third occurrence, confirming it is systematic in the handler rather than a per-app accident.

start_page::init::.S_FRONT.PARAMS.why: The port's PARAMS record for the start page view. Its XML also differs from upstream's beyond the envelope (attribute order and the displayBlock/height pair), which is tracked separately under the view-builder worklist item rather than here.

start_page::init::.S_FRONT.S_ACTION.why: The start page additionally issues a SET_FOCUS action in T_CUSTOM alongside the view in T_SYSTEM, which is the clearest evidence that the new envelope is ORDERED and multi-action: the port's PARAMS record has no way to express 'render this view, then focus that control' as a sequence.

start_page::init::view:MAIN.why: The start page views diverge from character 15 - different namespace order, a z2ui5.cc namespace only this port declares, and a different page title ("Developing UI5 Apps Pur..." vs upstream's "Build UI..."). Unlike hi_world this is not a missing attribute but two apps that have genuinely grown apart, so reconciling it needs a decision rather than a patch: does the port's start page follow upstream's, or is it openly its own app? Do not fix piecemeal before that is decided. (Until abap2UI5#2771 this question also covered the model, where upstream published its whole client graph under MODEL.CLIENT and the port a flat MS_HOME. Upstream stopped walking the client, the two models now agree in shape, and what is left of that difference is the two MS_HOME fields above - so the model half of this decision is smaller than it looked.)
start_page::init::view:MAIN.tracked: docs/adr-006-conformance.md — worklist item 2 (start page ownership decision)

unknown_app::init::.MODEL.why: Same cause — the port's fallback start page ships its model, upstream's 500 ships nothing. Third field of one accepted behavioural difference.

unknown_app::init::.S_FRONT.why: The consequence of the accepted fallback above: the port returns a whole S_FRONT (the start page) where upstream returns a non-JSON error body with no S_FRONT at all. Cannot be reconciled field by field while the fallback behaviour itself is intended.

unknown_app::init::.__error.why: Upstream answers an unresolvable app_start with HTTP 500 and an unhandled-exception page ('Request failed, no event (initial render)'); the port falls back to the start page. The port's behaviour is the better one for a web deployment — a mistyped URL should not 500 — and it is a deliberate platform adaptation, not a porting miss. Recorded as accepted so the difference is visible rather than invisible; revisit if upstream ever makes its own fallback graceful, because then the two should agree.

unknown_app::init::view:MAIN.why: The port renders its start page as the fallback for an unresolvable app_start; upstream 500s and renders no view at all, so there is nothing to compare against. Same accepted behavioural difference as the three unknown_app entries above — recorded per-slot because the view extraction reports slots independently of the envelope.
